item: review item: bind interoperability, timing and reproducibility results to one candidate

candidate.why: this is byte-identical to the DSO the four OpenSSH interop matrix cells link, so one artefact now carries the interop result, the ctgrind matrix, the dudect matrix and the branch audit

previously_reported_artifact.difference: the timing link omitted libcrypto.ld's version script; linking the same archive with the script reproduces ee7fa27c exactly, so the difference was the link only

ctgrind.toolchain: rustc 1.98.1, valgrind 3.19.0, in the same court invocation

cases.summary: 97626 errors from 111 contexts (a repeat run gave 96155 / 105)

ctgrind.variance: the ECDSA tests generate a key per run and the RSA test calls RSA_generate_key_ex, so the raw error totals vary; the stable quantities are the context counts (128, 20, 1, 0, 0) and the RSA contexts reproduced the reference 105 on a repeat run

dudect.flags_read_back: a0=0x4 a1=0x4 modulus=0x4 in all three flagged modes
dudect.controls_this_run: not run (no anomalous result required them); the controls from the previous run at a67305b1 are recorded in RECEIPT-dudect-modes.json

venue.court: docker/openssl-rs-court-tools:1, existing container, hard cap 6g/6g, 8 CPUs
venue.guard_note: host `available` was 21 GiB, below the 24 GiB line in AGENTS.md 6.1; the run used the already-capped court and reports the guard as not met rather than silently

limits: dudect state 1 is 'no leakage evidence yet', not a constant-time proof
the ECDSA signing ctgrind finding (128 contexts) and the RSA CRT finding (105-111 contexts) are unchanged by this re-measurement and remain the open findings
the branch audit establishes instruction shape in the audited ranges, not secret dependence
